title: Unsigned ordinary evaluation and its localization through the two augmentation comparisons
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived localization $Q$ with category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H=R\mathcal Hom$ with its fixed K-injective augmentations $\eta_F:F\to I(F)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix the closed symmetric monoidal structure and its canonical K-flat tensor and uncurrying models [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Write $\operatorname{tr}$ for its right-tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ for its counit. Write $O=\mathcal O[0]$ and also $O$ for its derived image. For arbitrary complexes $E,F$ put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,O)$. There is a unique chain map
$$a_{E,F}:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$$
whose component on local homogeneous sections $y\in F^p$, $\phi\in D^q$, $x\in E^a$ is $a_{E,F}(y\otimes\phi)(x)=y\phi(x)$ in $F^{a+p+q}$ when $a+q=0$, and is zero when $a+q\ne0$. Here the coefficient action and the identifications with degree zero of $O$ are the actual module-sheaf action and coefficient-unit identifications. The formula fixes the map on the sheafified pure-tensor generators, total-coproduct inclusions and all Hom-product projections. Define
$$\theta_{A,B}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((B\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(A,O))\otimes^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{\alpha}B\otimes^{\mathbf L}(H(A,O)\otimes^{\mathbf L}A)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{A,O}}B\otimes^{\mathbf L}O\xrightarrow{\rho}B\bigr).$$
Suppose $F,D$ are K-flat, and the maps $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_O)$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_F)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Let $\gamma_{E,G}:Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(QE,QG)$, for $G=O,F$, be induced by those augmentations and the fixed derived-Hom comparisons. Let $\mu:Q\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF\otimes^{\mathbf L}QD$ be the canonical K-flat tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then
$$\theta_{QE,QF}\circ(1\otimes\gamma_{E,O})\circ\mu=\gamma_{E,F}\circ Q(a_{E,F}).$$
In particular the ordinary formula has no Koszul sign. No K-flatness of $E$ or K-injectivity of $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08JD (lemma-dual), equation-eval (Tag 08JE), Tag 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), and section-hom-complexes; ordinary chain map and its fixed-augmentation derived comparison.

proof.text: Construct the graded map before imposing any flatness hypotheses. For each $p,q,a$, and on every localized site over $U$, send $(y,\phi)$ to the map $x\mapsto y\phi(x)$ if $a+q=0$, and to zero otherwise. Here $y$ is restricted along every object over $U$ before multiplication. This is bilinear over $\mathcal O|_U$, commutes with restrictions, and is linear in $x$, hence gives a section of the sheaf Hom. The presheaf tensor universal property followed by the unique sheafification factorization gives $F^p\otimes D^q\to\mathcal Hom(E^a,F^{a+p+q})$. The Hom-product universal property and then the total-coproduct universal property assemble these into $a^n$ for $n=p+q$. Those same universal properties imply uniqueness: equality can be checked after each total-summand inclusion, each Hom projection, and the presheaf-tensor sheafification unit. This uses all localized sections, not an assumption that every section of a sheaf tensor is globally a pure tensor.

Check the chain-map equation on the generators and projections of step 1. Regard $\phi$ as a homogeneous graded map $E\to O$ of degree $q$, zero in every unsupported component; since $d_O=0$, $d_D\phi=-(-1)^q\phi d_E$. Thus, writing $n=p+q$,
$$a(d_Fy\otimes\phi+(-1)^py\otimes d_D\phi)(x)=d_Fy\,\phi(x)-(-1)^{p+q}y\,\phi(d_Ex)=d_{\mathcal Hom(E,F)}(a(y\otimes\phi))(x).$$
The formula includes the case $a+q+1=0$, where the second term can be nonzero even though $\phi(x)=0$; all other unsupported terms vanish. By step 1's detecting maps this proves the chain equation and the asserted uniqueness as a chain map. The sign in the second term comes from the differentials, with no sign multiplying $y\phi(x)$.

source.place: section-hom-complexes, differential formula; Tag 08JE (equation-eval), ordinary representative calculation.

proof.text: Now assume $F,D$ are K-flat and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_O)$, $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_F)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $s:L\to E$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)$ and $W=\operatorname{Tot}(D\otimes L)$. The fixed model [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] says that $T$ and $W$ are K-flat. Also $O$ is K-flat: its degree-zero unit identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes O)$ with $A$, so it preserves acyclicity. Write $\mu_{X,Y}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}QX\otimes^{\mathbf L}QY$ for the fixed model on K-flat pairs, so $\mu_{F,D}$ is the specified $\mu$. The associator and unit constraints are induced by ordinary total-tensor constraints. We use the model on K-flat pairs as stated; we do not infer that $F$ or $D$ has flat terms from its K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), and fixed representative model for Tag 08J9.

proof.text:
Let $h_G=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_G)$, for $G=O,F$, and $h_{G,s}=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(s,I(G))h_G$. In the fixed representative coordinates the morphism
$$g_G:=H(Qs,1)\gamma_{E,G}:QD\to H(QL,QO)\quad(G=O)$$
(and with domain $Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$ and target $H(QL,QF)$ for $G=F$) is precisely $Qh_{G,s}$ followed by the fixed derived-Hom comparison. This is the functoriality of the recorded Hom construction in its first variable. The assumptions on $h_O,h_F$ make the two original $\gamma$ maps isomorphisms; $Qs$ is invertible because $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $H(Qs,1)$ is invertible because $H$ is a functor. In particular no claim that $\mathcal Hom(E,-)$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism is being made.

source.place: section-internal-hom, construction and localization factorization of RHom; fixed augmentations.

proof.text:
Define $v_s:W\to O$ by $v_s(\phi\otimes z)=\phi(sz)$ for homogeneous $z\in L^a$, interpreted as zero unless $a+q=0$. This is a chain map: on each tensor generator its differential condition is
$$(d_D\phi)(sz)+(-1)^q\phi(s\,d_Lz)=-(-1)^q\phi(d_Esz)+(-1)^q\phi(s\,d_Lz)=0.$$
It descends and is detected by the same sheafification and coproduct maps as in step 1. The actual uncurrying of $h_{O,s}:D\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(O))$ sends $\phi\otimes z$ to $\eta_O(\phi(sz))$, so it equals $\eta_Ov_s$. Apply the fixed uncurrying equation to the K-flat pair $(D,L)$. If $\operatorname{untr}$ denotes inverse closed transposition, it gives
$$\operatorname{untr}(g_O)=(Q\eta_O)^{-1}Q(\eta_Ov_s)\mu_{D,L}^{-1}=Qv_s\mu_{D,L}^{-1}=:e_s.$$
The cancellation uses the fixed augmentation, with no substitute choice of an identification of $QD$ with the dual.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose) and 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), fixed uncurrying normalization; evaluation calculation.

proof.text:
Apply the same fixed uncurrying equation to the K-flat pair $(T,L)$ and the chain map $h_{F,s}a:T\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,I(F))$. It supplies a chain map $b:\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes L)\to I(F)$ with its actual tensor-summand components prescribed by
$$b((y\otimes\phi)\otimes z)=\eta_F\bigl(y\phi(sz)\bigr).$$
Indeed this is exactly the evaluation of the Hom section $h_{F,s}(a(y\otimes\phi))$ at $z$, first applying $s$ and then the actual coefficient augmentation. Consequently
$$\operatorname{untr}(g_F\,Q(a))=(Q\eta_F)^{-1}Qb\,\mu_{T,L}^{-1}.$$
This use of the model has K-flat tensor source $T$ and K-flat second input $L$, and K-injective target $I(F)$; it does not assume $F$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), representative uncurrying into the fixed K-injective target; Tag 08JE (equation-eval).

proof.text:
Write $\alpha^{\rm ord}:\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes L)\to\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes W)$ and $\rho_F^{\rm ord}:\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes O)\to F$ for the ordinary associator and coefficient unit action, and put
$$c=\rho_F^{\rm ord}\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes v_s)\alpha^{\rm ord}.$$
Both $b$ and $\eta_Fc$ send $((y\otimes\phi)\otimes z)$ to $\eta_F(y\phi(sz))$. The ordinary associator only changes parentheses and the right unitor acts by the actual coefficient action; neither exchanges factors. Apply the detecting maps of step 1 twice to obtain $b=\eta_Fc$. Thus step 6 simplifies to
$$\operatorname{untr}(g_F Q(a))=Qc\,\mu_{T,L}^{-1}.$$
All cancellations are of localized augmentations, not chain-level inverses.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product), 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), and 08JE (equation-eval); actual associator and coefficient unit calculation.

proof.text:
Let $A=QE$, $B=QF$. By the definition of $\theta$ and naturality of the right-tensor adjunction in its source and tensor parameter, the inverse transpose of
$$H(Qs,1)\theta_{A,B}(1\otimes\gamma_{E,O})\mu_{F,D}$$
is
$$\rho_B(1_B\otimes e_s)\alpha_{B,QD,QL}(\mu_{F,D}\otimes1_{QL}).$$
Here counit naturality in the tensor parameter identifies the evaluation after $Qs$ with $\operatorname{untr}(H(Qs,1)\gamma_{E,O})=e_s$ from step 5. To compute this composite, use the induced associator constraint, naturality of the fixed tensor comparison on $v_s:W\to O$, and the induced right-unit constraint, respectively:
$$\alpha(\mu_{F,D}\otimes1)\mu_{T,L}=(1\otimes\mu_{D,L})\mu_{F,W}Q\alpha^{\rm ord},$$
$$(1\otimes Qv_s)\mu_{F,W}=\mu_{F,O}Q\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes v_s),\qquad \rho_B\mu_{F,O}=Q\rho_F^{\rm ord}.$$
Substitution of $e_s=Qv_s\mu_{D,L}^{-1}$ cancels $\mu_{D,L}^{-1}\mu_{D,L}$ and makes the displayed inverse transpose exactly $Qc\mu_{T,L}^{-1}$. Every comparison in these equations is on K-flat pairs from step 3. This writes out the compatibility with both augmentation comparisons rather than asserting an unspecified transport.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom) and 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), natural adjunction and induced associator/unit constraints; equation-eval (08JE).

proof.text:
Steps 7 and 8 have equal inverse transposes. The closed adjunction is a bijection, hence their maps into $H(QL,QF)$ agree. Cancel the isomorphism $H(Qs,1)$ of step 4 to obtain
$$\theta_{QE,QF}(1\otimes\gamma_{E,O})\mu_{F,D}=\gamma_{E,F}Q(a_{E,F}).$$
The construction in steps 1-2 did not need any flatness. In the comparison, only $F,D$ and the auxiliary resolution $L$ were required to be K-flat. The two stated augmentation quasi-isomorphisms supply exactly the two $\gamma$ isomorphisms; neither K-flatness of $E$ nor K-injectivity of $F$ entered.
